parts.title: My first audition
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last month, I went to an audition for a TV talent show. I sing and play the piano, and my friends had told me for years that I should try. I was very nervous, but I filled in the form and went to the city.

When I arrived, there were over a thousand people waiting outside. Some were dancing, some were singing, and one man was walking on his hands. I waited for five hours before it was my turn. My legs were shaking, and my throat was dry.

In the room, there were three judges. One of them asked, "What are you going to sing?" My voice was so quiet that she asked me to repeat it. Then I began, and after a few seconds, I forgot my fear. When I finished, the judges looked at one another. One of them smiled and said, "Thank you. You will hear from us."

I am still waiting for their answer. Even if they say no, I do not regret it. Walking into that room was the bravest thing that I have ever done, and I learned that I am stronger than I thought.

questions.explanation: She does not regret it; it was the bravest thing she has done.

parts.title: Behind the scenes of a talent show
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Talent shows look easy on TV, but a lot of hard work goes on behind the scenes. [1] Months before the show, a team of people starts to look for the best acts.

First, thousands of people are invited to audition. [2] Only a small group goes through to the next round, and the rest are told "thank you".

Then the acts practise with a coach. [3] The coach helps them to choose the right clothes, the right music and the best moment to start.

On the night of the live show, everything must be exactly on time. [4] A mistake of even a few seconds can ruin the programme for millions of viewers.

After the show, the winners may become famous overnight. [5] Experts say that it takes years of work to build a career in music or dance.
sentences: The producers use clocks and screens to check every moment.
But a TV prize does not always lead to lasting success.
The programmes often become famous around the world.
It is hard work for the crew, and nobody gets much sleep.
Some of the judges also work as music teachers.
Each of them performs for just a few minutes in front of the judges.
The first rule is that every minute on stage must be useful.
The winner is often chosen by the public, using their phones.

gaps.explanation: It is hard work for the crew, which fits the idea of work behind the scenes.
Each of them performs for a few minutes, and the next sentence says only a few go through.

parts.title: Stage fright
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Almost everybody feels nervous before they perform. Your heart beats faster, your hands become cold, and you may feel sick. This feeling is called stage fright. It is a natural reaction, and even famous actors suffer [1] it. The good news is that there are ways to deal with it. Firstly, practise as much [2] you can. When you know your song or speech very well, you will feel more confident. Secondly, breathe slowly and deeply before you go on stage. This helps to calm your body and [3] you think clearly. Thirdly, imagine that the audience is on your side. Most people want you to do well, [4] they will not laugh at a small mistake. Finally, remember that nobody else knows exactly what you planned to do. If you forget a line, simply smile and carry [5]. The audience will probably not notice anything. With time, you will enjoy being on stage much [6] than you fear it.

gaps.explanation: Suffer from it: the fixed preposition.
As much as you can: a fixed comparison.
Helps to calm your body and help you think clearly.
Most people want you to do well, and they will not laugh.
Carry on: phrasal verb meaning continue.
Enjoy it much more than you fear it.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Ladies and gentlemen, our next act is Izzy, and I must tell you a little story about her. Yesterday, she told me that she would sing her favourite pop song, but her voice goes strange when she is nervous, so she changed her mind. Then she wanted to tell some jokes, but her brother said that hers were terrible, and she believed him. In the end, she has been practising for a month with three coloured balls. She can keep them in the air for two minutes, and she hasn’t dropped them once in the last week. Please give her a big welcome, and let’s hope for the best!

question.prompt: What will the girl do in the show?
question.explanation: She changed her mind about singing and her brother said her jokes were terrible; she has practised for a month with three balls.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Good morning, students. This is a reminder about the final of the talent show. We first planned it for Friday afternoon, but that is the day of the school trip, so we had to cancel that idea. After that, we wanted Saturday evening, but the hall is booked for a wedding, so we can’t use it. That leaves Sunday. The final will be on Sunday morning at ten o’clock. The doors open at half past nine, and please remember that all the acts must be at the back of the hall at nine for a short rehearsal. See you then, and good luck!

question.explanation: Friday afternoon was cancelled because of the trip and Saturday evening because of a wedding, so the final is on Sunday morning.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Did you vote in the end? I gave my vote to the dancers.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I almost did the same. They were so quick! But my friend says they used a recording, so they didn’t really dance live.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What about the magician? Everyone was talking about him.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: He was funny, but the trick with the cards went wrong, so I’m afraid he lost my vote. I gave it to the band. The singer was fantastic.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’ll be honest, they were a bit loud.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s the point of a band!

question.prompt: Who did the girl vote for?
question.explanation: She nearly voted for the dancers but heard they used a recording, and the magician’s trick went wrong; she gave her vote to the band.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hale, you look pale. Are you ill?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m not ill. I sneezed this morning, but that’s only the dust in my room. And I’m not hungry, I had two big sandwiches at ten.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So what is it?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I was at the theatre rehearsing until midnight, and then I stayed up with my script. I got hardly any sleep, two hours at the most.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No wonder. Why don’t you go home early?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I might, after the lesson. I have a test at two, and I don’t want to miss it.

turns.speaker: f

question.prompt: Why does the boy look pale?
question.explanation: The sneeze is only dust and he ate two sandwiches; he rehearsed until midnight and had only two hours of sleep.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Tickets for Saturday’s show are on sale now at the school office. An adult ticket costs twelve pounds, and children under five come in for free. Last year students paid ten pounds, but this year we have a special price. If you show your school card, a student ticket is only eight pounds. You can buy as many as you like for your family, but remember that the hall holds two hundred people, and last year we sold out in two days. So don’t wait, because you will not find any tickets at the door.

question.explanation: Adults pay twelve and students paid ten last year, but this year the price with a school card is eight pounds.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Jace, you were so good in the school play. Do you want to sing professionally? Your voice is great.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Thanks. My mum would like that. But I only sing in the shower.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: A teacher then? You always help the little kids with their maths homework.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I enjoy that, but I do it because I’m good at maths. It’s not my dream. I want to be on a stage, in front of an audience, saying someone else’s words. I’d love to join the actors at the theatre in town. That’s what I felt in the play.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Well, you have my vote.

question.prompt: What does the boy want to be?
question.explanation: A singer and a teacher are not his dream; he wants to stand on a stage and say other people’s words, like the people at the theatre.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: The show finished at eleven! It was supposed to end at ten.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I know. At first I thought the singers took their time, but to be fair they were all quick.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: And the judges? They spoke a lot, but just a minute each, I counted.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: The real delay was at nine, when the microphones stopped. They tried for twenty minutes to fix the sound before the next act.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Oh yes, I forgot about that.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Me too, until the lights went off.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’m so nervous, Jace. My audition is in ten minutes, and I want to change my song.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: To what? You’ve practised the slow one for weeks.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: A fast one is more impressive. And the judges might fall asleep with a slow song.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Maybe, but you don’t know the fast one well. You forgot the words twice yesterday. Sing the one you love, the one you can do half asleep.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You’re right. I could ask to go tomorrow, but I’d be nervous anyway.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Exactly. Do your slow one.

question.explanation: He says she forgot the words of the fast one twice and that she was not better prepared tomorrow, so he advises the song she loves.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I can’t do it, Ivy. I’ll forget the words on stage and everybody will laugh.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Everybody forgets sometimes. Even actors on television. I was terrified in the school choir, my hands shook, and it always passed after the first minute.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You? I never knew.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Nobody did. That’s the point. You’ve learned your part and you know it very well. If you didn’t feel nervous, it would mean that you don’t care. I would worry if you weren’t.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: OK. Maybe I should leave the show.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No, don’t be silly. You’ll be fine.

options: It is normal and will pass
It shows that he is not ready
It is a reason to leave the show
question.explanation: She says everybody gets nervous, that it passed after a minute for her and that he knows his part; she tells him not to leave.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Ivor, I’m sorry. I know you wanted to win.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Honestly, I’m fine. Yes, I practised for months, and I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a bit disappointed, but only for a minute. The judges were fair. Her voice is much better than mine.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You’re not angry about the way they chose?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No way. I gave her a big hug when they said her name. The winner is my friend, and I’m so pleased for her after the year she’s had.

question.prompt: How does the man feel about the result?
question.explanation: He is disappointed for a minute only and thinks the judges were fair; he hugged his friend and is happy for her.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Jade, I love that song, but could you...? I’m learning my lines and I can’t hear myself think.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Do you want me to go to another room? I can take my speaker to the kitchen.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, no, stay. It’s your room too. And please don’t change the song. It’s the best part of my day. Just lower the music a little, then I can concentrate.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Sure, no problem. Like that?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Perfect. Thanks, Jade. You’re the best flatmate I’ve ever had.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Only because I’m the only one you’ve ever had!

question.prompt: What does the man want the woman to do?
question.explanation: He does not want her to go to another room or to change the song; he asks her to lower the music so that he can concentrate.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hale, the bus leaves in ten minutes and the costumes are still on the stage.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Shall we try them on again first? The red coat was too tight.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No time. We tried them yesterday, and it can be fixed at the theatre. And if we miss this bus the next one is in an hour.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So we carry everything now?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Yes. You take the big bag, and I’ll take the boxes. Quick!

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Wait, where are the keys of the van?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: In my pocket. Come on, the driver doesn’t like waiting.

question.prompt: What do the friends decide to do first?
question.explanation: There is no time to try on the costumes and the next bus is in an hour, so they take the bags and the boxes to the bus now.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Ivor, you look worried. Are we at the right door?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, this is the right door, and I’ve got money for the bus home in my wallet. The problem is that my ticket for the show was in my jacket, and I can’t find it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Did you check all your pockets?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Three times. If I’ve lost it, they won’t let me in, because the show is sold out.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Let’s ask at the desk. They have your name on the list.

options: Having no money for the bus

parts.title: A talk about a school talent show
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Hello, everyone. I’m Isla, and I’m in charge of this year’s talent show. First, the date. The show takes place on the twentieth of March in the school hall. Please don’t mix it up with the dress rehearsal, which is a week before, on the thirteenth. Last year we held the show in the sports hall, but this time the school hall is better because it has a proper stage. The doors open at half past six, but the show begins at seven, so please arrive early to find a seat. A record number of students wanted to take part. Last year there were twenty-two acts, and the show was far too long. So this year the judges chose eighteen of them. There are singers, dancers, two bands and a boy who plays the violin while he rides a unicycle. To keep the evening short, every act can last up to three minutes. The bands asked for five minutes, but I said no. Now for the tickets. An adult ticket costs four pounds. Children under twelve pay two pounds, and students from our school pay nothing if they show their card. You can buy them in the school office or at the door. Finally, the reason for it all. In the past we used the money for new books for the library, and one year for a school bus. This time we’ll give everything to the children’s hospital in town, because they need toys and games for the young patients. The parents’ group will also sell cakes and tea in the corridor, and they would like some help. So please bring your family and your friends. I hope you’re all as excited as I am. Thank you.

gaps.explanation: The rehearsal is on the thirteenth, but the show is on the twentieth.
The doors open at half past six, but the show begins at seven.

gaps.prompt: The judges chose ___ acts this year
gaps.explanation: Last year there were twenty-two acts, but this year the judges chose eighteen.

gaps.prompt: No act may last longer than ___ minutes
gaps.explanation: The bands asked for five minutes, but every act can last up to three minutes.

gaps.prompt: An adult pays ___ pounds to get in
gaps.explanation: Children pay two pounds and students nothing; an adult ticket costs four pounds.

gaps.prompt: The money will help sick children at the ___
gaps.explanation: In the past the money was for the library and a school bus, but this time it goes to the children’s hospital.

parts.title: An interview with a young singer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Jace, you became famous very fast. How did that feel?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Honestly, it was amazing, but it was strange. One week I was a normal student, and the next week people stopped me in the street to take photos. I’m not saying it was boring. I loved the attention, and I wasn’t tired of it, even though the days were long. But it felt like someone else’s life, and sometimes I looked in the mirror and asked who that was.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was the hardest part?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Everybody expects the early mornings to be the worst, and I do hate them, six o’clock every day. Meeting famous people was scary the first time, but you get used to it. The real killer was the schedule. Every Monday they gave me a new song, and by Saturday I had to know every word and every note, with the dancing too. I almost never slept on Fridays.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was it like with the other contestants?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It surprised me, because I expected a fight. Some of them were very funny, especially a girl from Wales who did impressions of the judges. And a boy taught me two dance moves, although I’m still bad at it. But what I valued most is that we helped each other. At night someone always had time to sit with you and go through a difficult line.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Did the judges give you any useful advice?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: One of them did, and I’ll never forget it. I was singing a song perfectly, with no mistakes, and she stopped me. She said, "Jace, I believe your voice, but I don’t feel anything." I thought I should choose easier songs, or practise less, but she told me that wasn’t the problem. What mattered was how I share a feeling with the people in the room.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What are you doing next month?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I had an offer to be in a film, and I read the script, but I said no, because I can’t act. A university has offered me a place, but I have asked to wait a year. So next month I start a tour of ten theatres, from Glasgow to Plymouth. I’m so excited, I can’t wait.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice would you give to a young person with the same dream?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Don’t do it to become famous. That might happen, and it might happen very quickly, but it isn’t a good reason. Listen to the judges, of course, but remember that they are only four people, and you must decide for yourself. Do it for the love of music. If you enjoy singing in your room, you will enjoy it on a big stage.

questions.prompt: How did Jace feel about being famous?

questions.explanation: He says it was not boring and he was not tired of it; it felt amazing and, at the same time, like somebody else’s life.

questions.prompt: What was the hardest part for Jace?

questions.explanation: He hates the early mornings and was afraid of famous people, but the real problem was a new song every Monday.

questions.prompt: Why did Jace value the other contestants?

parts.prompt: Your class wants to hold a talent show for parents. Talk about the different acts that you could have and decide which would be the best for the evening.

parts.title: Talk about the topic
parts.instructions: Answer the questions. Try to give a reason or an example with each answer.

questions.prompt: Do you think that talent shows are good for young people? Why?
Would you like to be famous? Why or why not?
What do you do to feel brave before a big event?
